correctness.rationale: After clearing denominators the equation is q(A+B-1)=(A-1)(2B-1) for A=2^a and B=2^b. Since gcd(A+B-1,A-1)=1, the common divisor A+B-1 divides both 2B-1 and 2A-1. Positivity forces A<=B and B<=A, hence A=B and q=A-1. The converse is direct. The finite exact-rational checker is corroborative only.

final_claim: A harmonious pair of the form (2^a,2^b q), with a,b positive and q odd prime, exists exactly when a=b and q=2^a-1 is prime.
limitations: The odd prime has exponent one; arbitrary odd prime powers or arbitrary friends of a power of two are not classified.
